turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

You entered a zero on Owen's essay a week ago, and he found out from his phone in the middle of a class. Nobody called me first. Before you say anything else, Hale, who decided that, and was Owen heard before you did it?
The checker said 94 percent. That's the end of it.

"That's the end of it." Your own school's procedure, 4.3, says software alone does not establish a concern, and I have the company's guide in my bag saying the same thing. So that's a machine's guess, and I'm writing down that it's all you've got.
I don't need more proof than that.
"I don't need more proof than that." Then you'll be saying it to the principal this afternoon, because I'm not leaving this building until that zero is withdrawn.
The software doesn't lie, unlike some people.
"Unlike some people." My son doesn't lie, Hale, so tell me plainly whether you're calling him a liar, or me. Either way, that sentence is going in my notes and then to the principal.

Then put it in an email tonight: who decided, on what date, on what basis, and whether Owen was heard first. You skipped 4.1 and 4.2, and I'm asking for a principal's review under 4.6 today. I'll be in that office in five minutes unless you have something on paper.
